page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Operating at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The processor features an extensive instruction set, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations and integer math.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in CPU-bound workloads. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the middle tier, while Geekbench evaluations show strong single-core and multi-core performance, particularly in software compilation and ray tracing. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in image and text processing. Cryptographic operations and database tasks also score highly, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI. For language model workloads, the platform achieves strong prompt processing speeds on small and medium models, alongside top-tier text generation throughput on small models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-48 offers a high-density compute profile. By limiting memory allocation to 2.0 GB per vCPU and omitting local storage, the instance minimizes overhead costs for workloads that are strictly CPU-bound. This resource balance makes it highly efficient for parallel processing tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and integrated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, rendering this instance unsuitable for large-scale database hosting requiring high local IOPS or heavy deep learning training.

This server is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, image and text processing pipelines, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for batch processing, cryptography, and parallelized simulation tasks.
